topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series and sets out the learning objectives regarding cancer causation and environmental carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Foundations of cancer etiology and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual foundations of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease, examining the balance between intrinsic mutations, environmental factors, and geographic variations in risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral and bacterial pathogens contribute to malignancy, illustrated through the multifactorial etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical compounds induce DNA damage directly or following metabolic activation by host enzymes.

topics.label: Tumor promotion and host susceptibility context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental stages cooperate with initiating mutations to drive tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for assessing carcinogenicity and mutational exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic signatures, epidemiological frameworks, and experimental model systems used to detect and evaluate carcinogens.

topics.label: Closing perspectives on carcinogenic risk and benefit
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure within everyday risk-benefit decisions.
